title: hw1/thresholds.json
description: The six numbers you derive, and the only place in the assignment a derived number may live. api.py reads this file at runtime; it is NOT in the repo, you author it. Nothing has a default: a threshold nobody derived is a threshold nobody can defend, so api.py raises rather than filling one in. The file is FLAT -- one band set for the whole assignment, not one per floor, because applying the floor-1 bands to your floor-2 capture and reporting whether they transferred IS the phase-2 deliverable. Two kinds of number live here and they are read at different times: tau_lo/tau_hi are MEASUREMENT parameters, read at insert time and baked into every stored clip fraction (change one and the store is stale -- re-run insert, which replaces the batch's named graph wholesale and is therefore safe to repeat); the four bands are GATING parameters, read at retrieve time (change one and you re-run retrieve, nothing else). NAMING: every band key is <observable_name>_<min|max>, so the key names the exact observable it bounds; the shorter spellings you will see on the retrieve CLI (--valid-depth-min, --roughness-max, --clip-hi-max, --clip-lo-max) are override FLAGS in a separate namespace and are not keys of this file. The Immerkaer kernel and its two constants, behind depth_roughness, are NOT here either: they are fixed by the measurement contract in api.py, not derived by you.

tau_lo.description: Shadow-clipping threshold on V = max(R,G,B). A pixel with V <= tau_lo has EVERY channel crushed. Must be < tau_hi. Read at insert time; recorded on the Batch node as hw1:tauLo, without which a stored clip fraction has no recoverable meaning.

tau_hi.description: Highlight-clipping threshold on V = max(R,G,B). A pixel with V >= tau_hi has AT LEAST ONE channel saturated. Must be > tau_lo. Read at insert time; recorded on the Batch node as hw1:tauHi.

bands.description: The four one-sided gates, all read at retrieve time and substituted into the FILTER of queries/valid_frames.rq. A frame passes only if it clears all four. They do NOT all point the same way: valid_depth_fraction_min is the only lower bound, the other three are upper bounds. None is a range. The _min / _max suffix on each key states its direction.

valid_depth_fraction_min.description: Keep frames with valid_depth_fraction >= this. More usable depth is better.

depth_roughness_max.description: Keep frames with depth_roughness <= this, in METRES. The observable is a reference-free estimate of the depth raster's noise standard deviation (Immerkaer 1996), so LOWER is better -- note the direction, this bound points the opposite way to valid_depth_fraction_min. A frame with no measurable window at all scores inf and is therefore rejected by any finite bound here. The maximum of 10 is only a sanity ceiling: a noise level above the sensor's whole usable range is a unit error, millimetres written where metres belong.

clip_hi_fraction_max.description: Keep frames with clip_hi_fraction <= this. Less blown-out is better. Meaningful only alongside the tau_hi it was measured at.

clip_lo_fraction_max.description: Keep frames with clip_lo_fraction <= this. Less crushed is better. Meaningful only alongside the tau_lo it was measured at.
